newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latam sugar 96-97 consumption seen at 21.4 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Latam sugar 96-97 consumption seen at 21.4 mln T.

text.p: Latin American sugar consumption is seen increasing to 21.4 million tonnes this crop year 1996-1997, up eight percent in three years, the senior analyst for tropical commodities of Sparks Companies Inc said Thursday.

Peter Buzzanell told the F.O. Licht World Sugar and Sweetners' Conference here that Latin American consumption has been trending upwards for the last 20 years, basically on the back of population growth.

Buzzanell said for the decade ending 1994-1995, the region's sugar use expanded 23 percent to 20.5 million tonnes. That was slower growth than seen from the 12.2 million tonnes in the mid- 1970s to 16.7 million tonnes in the mid-1980s, a 37 percent increase.

Looking forward, Buzzanell said he expected growth to continue in the region. "For the region as a whole, total sugar consumption is forecast at 22.8 million tonnes (for the year 2001-2002) and again will help underpin expected growth in global demand," he said.

Buzzanell reiterated that the major factor in the expansion of sugar use would be continued population growth, forecast to climb to 530 million by the 2001-02 year from the 495 million currently in Latin America.
